title: Reachable public hierarchy
setup_and_action: F-OBJECT: on an independently initialized owned patch and available Live context, identify one eligible ordinary object and its documented child using independently accepted path/metadata. Retain target/source identity; missing member does not prove generic failure.
source_claim: The public overview describes a hierarchy of Live objects with single children and object lists, exposing only part of Live. Reachability, available members and types must be independently established; the inventory is not all application internals or complete API closure.

title: Path syntax and relative context
setup_and_action: F-PATH: identify a valid nonempty list/member and known current position, then compare accepted absolute and relative routes on reset copies. Retain actual path/object identity; no numeric ID or parser-output oracle.
source_claim: Overview paths are unquoted navigation terms with zero-based list indices; more than one path may identify the same object. Relative paths begin from current hierarchy position. These source roles do not prescribe a complete argument grammar, quote parser or native index encoding.

title: Root families
setup_and_action: F-PATH: retain accepted device/Set/application context and independently available root for each actually offered category; controller root requires accepted controller setup. Navigate only valid known roots; absent capability remains U.
source_claim: The overview/path reference names live_app, live_set, control_surfaces with an index and this_device as root roles. Control-surface access depends on the controller; this_device is device-relative. Root availability, identity and lifetime are not universal constants.

title: Canonical path and parent roles
setup_and_action: F-PATH/F-OBJECT: independently identify one object through two eligible routes, request canonical path/parent, then repeat with nested rack/device context only if available. Capture returned identity/path; no parent topology or ordering oracle.
source_claim: Multiple paths can lead to one object; the overview describes a unique canonical path, returned by live.object getpath, and a get-only canonical_parent child. Its own-track example is not an unconditional parent-is-track law for nested devices or roots.

title: Object IDs and no-object sentinel
setup_and_action: F-IDENTITY: retain a positively resolved owned object and separate no-object context; move/reorder, duplicate and delete/recreate only owned objects on separate copies. Record actual paths/IDs without exact numbers, monotonicity, reuse, persistence or lifetime comparator.
source_claim: The overview describes id plus integer tokens, with id 0 denoting no object, device-scoped IDs assigned when navigated, normally stable while an object exists, and possible move-as-delete/create exceptions. Deletion/replacement and nonreuse/nonstorage prose are documentary contexts, not target ID allocation or durable identity laws.

title: Children, properties and call roles
setup_and_action: F-OBJECT: independently establish one list, one existing single child, one absent child, one readable property and separately writable/observable/callable member. Probe each only with known admissible inputs; no complete member capability table is supplied.
source_claim: Types describe available children/properties/functions; children may be single, lists or absent. getcount applies to lists, while get/set and call access eligible state/functions. Not all children/properties are observable or settable. Individual LOM member capability remains separately unresolved.

title: Notifications versus polling
setup_and_action: F-OBSERVE: establish a valid object/property and positive explicit lookup and change baseline. Separately poll and change state through an accepted UI action; retain spontaneous versus requested messages without timing or count equality.
source_claim: The overview distinguishes explicit navigation/get/call polling from spontaneous notifications for path-object changes and property values. This supplies event roles only, not cadence, coalescing, delivery order, queue policy or a complete notification set.

title: Notification mutation context
setup_and_action: F-OBSERVE: with independently productive observed changes and a separately valid writable owned target, compare read-only handling and an attempted supported mutation from notification versus an independently available deferred action. No error string, scheduling or success oracle.
source_claim: Overview and observer prose says Live Set changes cannot be triggered directly while receiving notifications, and suggests deferred interaction in relevant contexts. This is a documented restriction/caution, not a prescribed candidate thread, queue architecture or guaranteed deferlow cure.

title: Navigation and path following outlets
setup_and_action: F-PATH: positively resolve owned object, bind another bridge from the appropriate output in an independently valid patch, then change a dynamic selection and separately remove the pointed-to object. Capture identities/messages without callback order or numeric expected ID.
source_claim: live.path selects objects for other bridges; its left output gives navigation identity and middle output follows the object currently at the path. A nonexistent path is described as yielding no-object IDs rather than an error. Path following is distinct from retaining one particular object.

title: Initial path and absolute path message
setup_and_action: F-INIT/F-PATH: after independently confirmed initialization compare explicit path navigation with a declared initial path on reset owned patch instances. Keep valid root/member fixed; do not use loadbang as readiness proof.
source_claim: live.path accepts an optional initial path and a path message for root-starting absolute paths. Root/name acceptance and initialization readiness remain target U; the initial argument is not proof of a ready Live API during patch load.

title: goto relative/up and list-member boundary
setup_and_action: F-PATH: valid nonempty current object/list and admitted member first, then compare relative child, up and list-container versus member requests in separate trials. Probe this_device only as unresolved context, no generic refusal or repair oracle.
source_claim: goto is documented for absolute or relative paths and up, selecting individual list members rather than the list itself. Its root list omits this_device while other source contexts include it; the omission does not settle that root’s goto acceptance.

title: Count and child enumeration
setup_and_action: F-OBJECT/F-PATH: known valid nonempty list and independent child inventory, then empty-list copy. Request count/children and retain raw output with actual source structure; no numeric count or order comparator.
source_claim: getcount reports a named list child’s count via the right outlet; getchildren reports available child names there. These are documented output roles, not stable list ordering, inherited-member closure or exact tuple/empty representation for target builds.

title: Current path response
setup_and_action: F-PATH: identify two accepted aliases for same owned object and a valid relative navigation; request path and separately object canonical path on reset trials. Retain strings without quote, normalization or alias-equality oracle.
source_claim: live.path getpath reports its current navigation path via the right outlet. This differs from live.object canonical getpath and does not require path spelling to match a canonical alias.

title: Combined bang/getid documented role
setup_and_action: F-PATH: independently valid current object then a known nonexistent path, invoke the explicitly documented combined-section context and retain outputs. Standalone placeholder interpretation and outlet sequencing are separate U probes.
source_claim: The combined bang, getid section describes emitting current-path identity through left and middle outputs, with no-object sentinel when absent. The separate standalone getid section is a placeholder and remains unsupported; no blank is filled from memory.

title: Select current object by ID
setup_and_action: F-OBJECT: retain positive readable target resolved in same independently valid device context, bind through each actually supported inlet in separate copies, then inspect current binding via an independent query. Numeric/message-order/error outputs remain null.
source_claim: live.object operates on selected Live objects; id assignment is described for either inlet, with right-inlet use suggested for clarity and no assignment output described. This is not input routing, ID scope or rejection parity for arbitrary tokens.

title: Current identity and type
setup_and_action: F-OBJECT: independently valid bound target and separate unbound instance; request identity/type and capture raw responses. Delete only owned target in separate U trial; no expected numeric ID or type-completeness oracle.
source_claim: getid or bang/getid reports current identity and gettype its object class; getid describes no-object when unbound. These output roles do not specify every invalid/deleted-ID branch, exact names or message interleaving.

title: Canonical getpath and getinfo roles
setup_and_action: F-OBJECT: positive valid object, request path/info, retain full raw response and separately known identity. Repeat a second supported object type; do not compare against the 588 direct-heading inventory as a complete runtime surface.
source_claim: getpath reports canonical current-object path. getinfo describes identity/type/description/children/properties/functions and a terminating done role, with repeatable description lines. No fixed line order/cardinality or complete inherited-member specification follows.

title: Read child versus child list
setup_and_action: F-OBJECT: valid object with independently known single child and nonempty list, query each then an empty/absent copy. Retain actual returned tokens only; no list order/count/ID expected value.
source_claim: get on an eligible list child reports element IDs; on a single child it reports that child ID. Source examples are not exact runtime IDs, alias names, empty-list formatting or universal child availability laws.

title: Read value versus value list
setup_and_action: F-OBJECT: independently readable scalar and list property on owned eligible objects; request each at two admitted states. Capture raw values/labels without native-enum, stored-unit, quoting or numeric equality oracle.
source_claim: get reads single-value and list properties, with types and capabilities delegated to the LOM. Example routing labels, names and numbers do not override current native/domain owners or define a complete return grammar.

title: Set child versus child list
setup_and_action: F-MUTATE: independently verified writable owned child/list capability and valid same-context identities, positive readback first; perform one admitted change then restore only through accepted actions. No hidden writable member or transaction/silence law is invented.
source_claim: set has separate single-child and child-list roles accepting eligible object identities. Not all children are writable; no assignment response is described. Complete mutation, list ordering, cross-device IDs and rollback remain U.

title: Set property versus value list
setup_and_action: F-MUTATE: separately admitted writable scalar/list property and independently valid values with positive target/readback baseline; attempt each on reset copies. Unavailable capability remains unmet prerequisite; no value, error or undo comparator.
source_claim: set writes eligible single/list property values; not all properties can be set and their types come from the LOM. No assignment response is described. Bounds, clamping, serialization, automation ownership and numerical conversion require separate evidence.

title: Function call role
setup_and_action: F-MUTATE: independently known supported callable member on disposable owned object and admissible argument set, with observable positive baseline first. Capture return and owned before/after state, no source example executed or generic function semantics inferred.
source_claim: call names a current-object function and optional typed parameters, with result output described by the public source. Actual callable members, signatures, side effects, return types and errors are not completed by this generic bridge clause.

title: Persistent Mapping Inspector option
setup_and_action: F-PERSIST: independently available initialized bridge and valid binding; inspect named option for each of the three bridges and retain actual selected state. Save/reopen/editor-move effects are separate null probes, not this visible-option comparison.
source_claim: live.object, live.observer and live.remote~ references name an Inspector Use Persistent Mapping option. Its save/restore/editor-move association prose is retained separately from overview/JS dynamic-ID cautions; default, cross-run numeric ID and exact-target persistence remain U.
documentary_expected: The named Use Persistent Mapping Inspector option is offered for the indicated bridge object; binding and persistence outcomes remain ungraded.
documentary_comparator: Inspect only the named visible option and actual selected setting; no ID, persistence, message, timing or runtime equivalence oracle.

title: Observe eligible property and changes
setup_and_action: F-OBSERVE: independently supported observable property and same-context valid object; positively read value, select observation and change property through admitted external UI action. Capture current/change output without immediate-delivery or exactly-once oracle.
source_claim: live.observer selects an eligible object/property and describes initial/current value plus later change notifications through its left output. An optional argument selects property/child. Not all properties are observable and notification timing/count/order are unproven.

title: Observe single child versus child list
setup_and_action: F-OBSERVE: independently eligible single child/list and positive nonempty observation, then separate empty/absent states through owned UI changes. Retain actual responses, not a universal silence, list or ID comparator.
source_claim: Observer property selection can target an observable child ID or child list; single-child source mentions no-object and list source permits no output for an empty result. Capability and representation differ and are not generalized to every child.

title: Binding and bang role
setup_and_action: F-OBSERVE: establish active valid observation and nonzero positive changing target first, then separate no-property/no-object/mismatched context and bang. Retain matched positive response; missing baseline cannot prove no-effect.
source_claim: Observer ID assignment accepts either inlet with right suggested; bang queries current selected property/object. The source describes no action without matching property/object, but invalid tokens, deleted objects and no-effect behavior remain target U.

title: Observer metadata outputs
setup_and_action: F-OBSERVE: valid property, single child and list selections separately; query metadata while keeping independently positive observation. Capture raw right/left outputs without enum, type-union or event-order expected value.
source_claim: getproperty, gettype and getid describe current selection/type/identity through observer right output, distinct from value output left. Child-list type information is described as limited; no complete typed schema or cross-outlet order follows.

title: DeviceParameter binding and release
setup_and_action: F-REMOTE: independently eligible DeviceParameter with active nonzero input/base/output and known working remote response first; compare valid, separately known nonparameter and release contexts on reset copies. No hidden ID/class mapping or release-time/value oracle.
source_claim: live.remote~ binds a DeviceParameter identity through the right inlet, describes no effect for non-parameter IDs, reports mapped identity via getid, and uses id 0 to release control/re-enable parameter. Nonparameter rejection, release ordering and restoration stay U.

title: Parameter LOM path UI entry
setup_and_action: F-REMOTE: independently admitted editable/eligible parameter and initialized owned context; inspect actually offered Copy LOM Path and retain copied text separately from accepted binding. No clipboard grammar or full live.map contract is supplied.
source_claim: The reference describes Copy LOM Path in a parameter context menu as available in Live 12, and live.path or live.map as ways to select a parameter. This does not specify the separate live.map object, exact path alias, menu eligibility for every control or target-build support.

title: Message and signal control roles
setup_and_action: F-REMOTE: active eligible parameter, independently valid nonzero signal/message path and positive source/output baseline. Compare each input family at two admitted values and actual supported rate/block settings separately; numeric/timing/signal responses null.
source_claim: Integer/float messages and signal input address the selected parameter through left inlet. Source prose distinguishes buffer/ramp scheduling from realtime signal application; sample-accurate/single-buffer claims are context, not target timing or candidate architecture requirements.

title: Ramp and smoothing controls
setup_and_action: F-REMOTE: known active positive remote path and admitted nonzero ramp settings; request one ramp then another during it, separately change actually offered smoothing. Capture control/audio traces with no linearity, latency, count or numerical output oracle.
source_claim: smoothing describes event ramp time and signal temporal sampling; a value/time list requests a ramp and a new ramp overrides a current ramp. No source default/example is promoted to target interpolation, sample count, rate law or interruption arithmetic.

title: Normalized-mode role
setup_and_action: F-REMOTE: independently known eligible parameter and admitted input/base/depth in both actual offered modes, positive remote response and output first. Capture mode/values without assuming native min/max/enum/gain conversion or clipping.
source_claim: normalized toggles between source-described automatic parameter-range scaling and caller-supplied parameter-domain values. This is not a conversion formula, native/stored-unit equivalence, valid range for every target or complete parameter behavior law.

title: Automation, undo and envelope context
setup_and_action: F-REMOTE/F-AUTO: independently active eligible parameter with nonzero source/output and separately changing automation/modulation baseline, explicit transport and recording state. Bind/drive/release remote on reset copies, retain exposed state/history/output with no arbitration or persistence oracle.
source_claim: Remote control is described as disabling parameter interaction/automation without changing saved Set value or creating Undo steps, while reference prose also says envelopes remain active. Automation versus envelope identity and restoration are unresolved contexts, not a blanket disable-all law.

title: Initialization and reload notification
setup_and_action: F-INIT: independently accepted owned device/patch and Live context; retain device load, preset load and save/reload as separate trials with readiness observation. No patch is created/executed here and no callback time/count/order oracle is supplied.
source_claim: live.thisdevice describes left-outlet bang when the Max device/containing patcher is opened and completely initialized, including Live API in the JS/overview context, and again for preset load or device save/reload. Generic loadbang is not proof of Live API readiness.

title: Enabled and preview state context
setup_and_action: F-INIT: independently accepted in-Live device then separate valid editor/Max context if available, known enabled/preview state and positive output first. Change each state and request getstate; raw numeric/outlet/order outputs remain null.
source_claim: Description distinguishes device-enabled middle output and preview right output in Live, with inactive state outputs when used in Max alone. getstate text says device state on rightmost output, leaving exact state meaning/context unresolved rather than merging enabled and preview.

title: Explicit bang and mouse entry
setup_and_action: F-INIT: independently ready owned device first, then separate not-yet-established context only if observable. Compare explicit message and double-click to automatic load notification, retaining readiness separately without equating them.
source_claim: Explicit bang, double-click and loadbang message roles describe left bang output. Those manual/message actions do not imply the device/API has reached the automatic complete-initialization condition.

title: Device width message and save caveat
setup_and_action: F-INIT: independently valid visible device with retained layout, use two actually admitted widths and offered reset separately, then save/reopen as U branch. No pixel, stored width or atomic resize comparator.
source_claim: setwidth changes Max for Live device width and its source says this is not automatically saved in preset/Set; the reset setting returns width calculation from visible objects. Exact pixels/default sizing, persistence mechanism and unrelated layout behavior remain unknown.

title: Initialized JavaScript access context
setup_and_action: F-JS/F-INIT: independently valid owned js-containing patch and accepted Max/Live configuration, initialized via accepted lifecycle context. Inspect offered API access separately from global/premature use; no script or example is executed in this packet.
source_claim: LiveAPI offers js access to path/object/observer roles, with source cautions against global-code use and high-priority execution and a live.thisdevice readiness recommendation. Legacy constructor context is retained. No JS engine version, scheduler architecture or full runtime compatibility is imposed.

title: Constructor and callback roles
setup_and_action: F-JS: independently valid initialized owned patch with eligible path/object and positively changing observable property. In separate accepted instances compare callback/path/identity contexts, retaining invocation/data without constructing a source example or imposing order.
source_claim: Constructor accepts optional callback and path or valid API identity; callback is described for referred-object or observed-property changes. Complete overload grammar, callback values/reentrancy and cross-instance ID acceptance are unresolved.

setup_and_action: F-JS/F-IDENTITY: two independently identified owned tracks/devices, accepted modes and positive binding before reorder. Compare object/location after each separate move and replacement; mode codes and callback/ID results stay null.
source_claim: LiveAPI mode distinguishes following the particular referred object across movement from following the object occupying a hierarchy location. Source defaults/examples are not exact-target numeric mode, move-as-recreate, ID lifetime or bank-selection laws.

setup_and_action: F-JS/F-PATH: positive valid object/path, alternate quoted/unquoted representation and accepted nonexistent path in separate trials. Reopen Set and re-resolve as U branch; no stored-ID equality, raw grammar or transient-validity comparator.

Complete grammar, validity timing and persistent bindings remain U.

title: Children and info/type metadata
setup_and_action: F-JS/F-OBJECT: independently known valid object and separately nonempty/empty child lists, request supported metadata in accepted initialized context. Capture raw types/arrays/counts without full-schema or numeric expected result.
source_claim: children/getcount expose current-path child information; info/type describe object metadata and patcher identifies containing context. These bridge roles do not complete inherited member semantics, child cardinalities, source code architecture or exact class/type unions.

setup_and_action: F-JS/F-MUTATE: independently admissible readable scalar/list/symbol and separately writable/callable owned members, with positive baseline. Compare get/getstring and one accepted write/call on reset copies; no script, source example or generic type parser is invented.
source_claim: JS get/getstring read property values/lists with distinct described representations; set writes and call invokes eligible members. Printed get type annotation is narrower than the generic description; complete return unions, member signatures, type conversion and errors require separate evidence.

setup_and_action: F-JS/F-OBSERVE: independently eligible observable property/child/list and positive binding/change baseline; select and externally mutate each separately. Capture callback/proptype without exactly-once, ordering or read/write-in-callback success oracle.
source_claim: property selects an observed property, child or child list and proptype describes selected type; callback changes are documented roles only. Capabilities, initial callback timing, mutation while handling and stale targets remain unresolved.

setup_and_action: F-IDENTITY: two owned positive objects; reorder/move, duplicate, delete/recreate and replace at same path in separate trials, then re-resolve. Preserve device/Set/root/mode context; no exact ID allocation/reuse or callback-order comparator.

setup_and_action: F-PATH/F-OBJECT: after a valid positive request attempt abc/empty/quoted/incomplete paths, wrong arity/type and NaN/out-of-range values only through independently understood accepted interfaces on test-owned targets. No arbitrary LOM member or hidden input codec is invented.

setup_and_action: F-INIT: compare initialized auto-load callback with manual bang/loadbang, save/preset reload and separate enabled/preview changes plus getstate. Retain actual Live versus editor/Max context; no outlet-state identity or immediate readiness guarantee.

No cadence, buffer latency, smoothing or phase equivalence law.

Capture manual/automation/remote/undo/saved state without merging envelopes and automation or numerical identity.

setup_and_action: F-REMOTE: independently productive DeviceParameter control with active nonzero source/base/depth/output first. Compare accepted nonparameter/invalid/unbound identities and id0 release separately, preserving paired positive baseline. No missing output or stale prior parameter proves no-effect.

setup_and_action: F-MUTATE: before-inventory of owned target/path/binding, perform one valid get/set/call/observer/remote or persistence change per reset copy then offered Undo/Redo. No generic history grouping or saved-value restoration law.

setup_and_action: F-MUTATE/F-REMOTE: begin actually offered parameter/patch edit, ramp or mapping selection and use supported cancellation/release before and after recorded commit in separate copies. No asynchronous API cancel command or rollback is invented.

setup_and_action: F-OBJECT/F-OBSERVE: independently valid object and positive observation/change, then overlapping external edit/reorder/selection while a request or ramp is pending in separate copies. No snapshot consistency, atomicity or caller priority law.

setup_and_action: F-OBJECT/F-OBSERVE/F-REMOTE: established positive valid target/binding/output first, delete only owned parameter device, clip/track or replace Set while active. Retain path/ID/observations and other active paths; no observer-reset, restoration or silence deadline.

setup_and_action: F-INIT: independently available accepted Live/editor context first; make only owned patch/context temporarily unavailable through supported controls, restore then re-resolve valid paths. No Max installation, fake host/API, recoverable-ID assumption or synthesized runtime is used.

setup_and_action: F-REMOTE/F-OBSERVE: positive active callback/observer or nonzero remote ramp/output; separately close device/patch, save-and-edit transition, close/replace Set or quit through offered controls. Capture prompts/output/state if available; no flush/cleanup/transaction deadline.
